documents.title: Gout / DM follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rheum note reviewed: gout with erosions on the right knee film, uric acid 9.2 at the flare. Now on allopurinol 100 and colchicine 0.6 daily. No flares since October. No diarrhea on the colchicine. No rash.
Angina unchanged and predictable. DM: home fastings 120s-140s.
Exam: BP/HR as charted. Knees quiet, no tophi. Heart regular. Lungs clear.
Labs: uric acid 7.6 on 100 mg. Creatinine and LFTs ok. A1c 7.0.
Plan: allopurinol to 200 mg daily (2 x 100 mg). Keep colchicine daily. Recheck uric acid in about 10 weeks. Asked him to go easy on the ibuprofen given his heart and kidneys; he uses it rarely now.

documents.title: Uric acid result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with pt. Uric acid 6.5 on 200 mg, still above the target of 6. Creatinine stable. Going to allopurinol 300 mg once daily, single tablet, new Rx sent; finish or discard the 100s. Continue colchicine through May. No flares.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seven weeks on allopurinol 300. No flares since October. Colchicine has been daily since late November, so six months done: stopping it today. Told him to text if a joint flares.
Otherwise unchanged. Angina only with real exertion.
BP/HR fine. Exam unremarkable.
Uric acid today under 6, at goal. Physical next month with full labs.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Feels well overall. Angina stable, only on hills or heavy lifting, rests and it goes. Cardiology f/u last fall, no changes. Gout quiet on allopurinol 300; off colchicine a month, no flare. Bowels normal since Whipple treatment.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, allopurinol 300, ibuprofen 400 prn (rarely). NKDA.
Exam: BP/HR as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Knees without effusion. Feet: sensation intact, pulses present, skin ok.
A/P: chronic issues stable; annual labs drawn. PCV20 today given diabetes. Colonoscopy due 2024. Flu/COVID booster in the fall.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED visit 11/02/2022, regional hospital.
CC: sudden palpitations with chest pressure, lightheadedness and shortness of breath.
Hx: abrupt onset at work. Substernal pressure, no radiation. Known CAD with stable angina followed by cardiology. Meds per list: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, metoprolol succinate, allopurinol, ibuprofen PRN. NKDA.
VS: BP 85/50, HR 180, RR 22, SpO2 92% RA.
Exam: JVP elevated; crackles at both bases.
ECG: wide-complex tachycardia, no P waves seen.
Labs: Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 1.1, troponin I elevated.
Course: IV access, O2. Unstable; procedural sedation and synchronized cardioversion to sinus rhythm. Admitted to cardiology.
Dx: unstable wide-complex tachycardia, likely VT.

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size. LVEF 55% by biplane Simpson. No regional wall motion abnormality. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Mitral, aortic, tricuspid and pulmonic valves structurally normal without significant regurgitation or stenosis. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Normal LV size and systolic function, LVEF 55%. No wall motion abnormality. Normal valves.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Admitted 11/02/2022, discharged 11/06/2022.
Dx: hemodynamically unstable ventricular tachycardia, cardioverted in the ED.
Course: monitored without recurrence. Echo LVEF 55%, no wall motion abnormality, valves normal. Coronary angiography 11/03: LAD stenosis about 70%, unchanged from 2020, no acute lesion. Single-chamber ICD implanted 11/04 for secondary prevention, left pectoral; device check before discharge normal.
Discharge meds: unchanged home regimen.
Follow-up: device clinic 2-3 weeks for wound check, cardiology 1 month. No driving for 6 months per state guidance. No lifting the left arm above shoulder for 4 weeks.

documents.title: In the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know I'm in the hospital since yesterday. Heart went racing at work, they had to shock it back. They're putting in a defibrillator tomorrow. Feeling ok now, just shaken up.

documents.title: Re: In the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, Kurt. Glad you're stable. Ask them to send me the records. Once you're home let's get you in within a week or two.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after admission 11/2-11/6. Only the ED sheet is here so far; history from patient. Sudden racing heart at his desk, felt faint and short of breath; shocked back in the ED. Told it was VT. Angiogram showed the same LAD narrowing as 2020, nothing new. Defibrillator placed 11/4. Meds unchanged at discharge.
Since home: no palpitations, no shocks, no fainting. Usual angina only with exertion. Wife driving him; he knows about the driving restriction.
Exam: BP/HR as charted. Left chest device pocket clean, dry, no hematoma, steri-strips on. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
BMP and Mg today.
A/P: VT, s/p cardioversion and ICD. Continue metoprolol succinate 50, other meds unchanged. Device clinic wound check next week. Requested discharge summary. Med rec done.

events.reason: Acute shortness of breath and chest discomfort

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Left chest single-lead cardiac device with lead tip in the right ventricle. Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Enlarged left atrium. No pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates with an enlarged left atrium.

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia. No ST-segment elevation or depression.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED 11/01/2023.
59M with CAD (stable angina, medical therapy), VT s/p ICD 2022, HTN, DM. Became short of breath and had chest discomfort walking to the grocery store; rapidly worse over an hour. Lightheaded, cannot lie flat. No known valve disease.
VS: BP 98/60, HR 112, RR 28.
Exam: diaphoretic, anxious. JVD to the angle of the mandible sitting up. New soft blowing holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla. Bibasilar crackles. No peripheral edema.
CXR: bilateral infiltrates, enlarged left atrium. ECG: sinus tachycardia, no ST elevation or depression.
Tx: supplemental O2, IV furosemide. Pulmonary artery catheter placed for hemodynamic monitoring. Echo ordered. Cardiology and cardiac surgery consulted; admitted to CCU.
Impression: acute mitral regurgitation with pulmonary edema.

reports.text: LV normal in size, hyperdynamic. LVEF 65% by biplane Simpson. Flail posterior mitral leaflet with ruptured chordae. Severe mitral regurgitation, eccentric jet. Left atrium enlarged. RV normal size and function. Aortic valve normal. Device lead in the right heart. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Severe mitral regurgitation due to flail posterior leaflet with ruptured chordae. LVEF 65%.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
Admission 11/01/2023 to 11/10/2023.
Dx: acute severe mitral regurgitation, flail posterior leaflet with ruptured chordae.
Course: diuresed in CCU with PA catheter monitoring. Echo as above, LVEF 65%. Mitral valve repair with annuloplasty ring 11/03/2023 via median sternotomy. Uncomplicated recovery. Post-repair echo: trace mitral regurgitation, ring well seated. ICD interrogated perioperatively, functioning normally.
Discharge meds: home regimen unchanged.
Follow-up: cardiac surgery 2 weeks, cardiology 6 weeks. Sternal precautions 6-8 weeks.

documents.title: Wife calling
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's wife called. He was taken to the ED yesterday, very short of breath, they found a leaking heart valve and he's in the cardiac unit. Surgeons planning to repair the valve tomorrow. Message to PCP. Asked her to have the hospital fax records.

documents.title: PCP call back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called wife back. Explained what we know, offered support. Will book a visit once he's home.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up after mitral valve repair

documents.title: Post-op visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Home since 11/10 after mitral valve repair (ring) on 11/3 for a torn chord and a flail leaflet, per patient and wife; ED sheet only in chart, summary requested. Breathing back to normal, sleeping flat. Sternum sore but improving. Walking the hallway and driveway.
Meds unchanged from before.
Exam: BP/HR as charted, afebrile. Sternotomy incision healing, no drainage or redness, sternum stable. Heart regular, no murmur heard today. Lungs clear. No edema. Weight down a few pounds.
BMP/CBC today.
A/P: acute MR s/p repair, recovering. Sternal precautions. Cardiac surgery and cardiology follow-ups booked. Med rec done.
